## Purpose

This SOP provides instructions for setting up RStudio, connecting it
to GitHub, and managing collaborative research projects using version
control. R [@rcoreteam2024], RStudio [@posit2024], and GitHub
[@github2024] together enable collaborative, transparent, reproducible,
and accessible data analysis. For a comprehensive practical guide, see
[@bryan2023].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All EA Program researchers using R for data analysis
  and collaborative projects
- **Does not apply to:** Local-only R scripts with no version control;
  Python or other language workflows
- **Location:** RStudio Server at Pomona College; local installations

## Definitions

- **R:** A free, open-source programming environment for statistical
  computing, maintained by a global community of statisticians and
  programmers [@rcoreteam2024].
- **RStudio:** A user interface for R that provides tools to write
  code, view results, manage files, and integrate with version control.
  Available as a desktop application or via the Pomona College server
  [@posit2024].
- **GitHub:** A web-based hosting service for Git repositories that
  enables collaborative code and document management [@github2024].
- **Repository (repo):** A GitHub project folder that contains all
  files, history, and collaboration settings.
- **Version control:** A system that tracks changes to files over time,
  allowing multiple people to collaborate while maintaining a complete
  history of who changed what and when.
- **SSH key:** A cryptographic key pair used to establish a secure
  connection between RStudio and GitHub without entering a password
  each time.
- **Clone:** Creating a local copy of a GitHub repository on your
  computer or server.
- **Branch:** A parallel line of development that lets you work on a
  feature or fix without affecting the main codebase until you are
  ready to merge.
- **Pull:** Downloading the latest changes from GitHub to your local
  copy.
- **Commit:** Saving a snapshot of your changes with a descriptive
  message.
- **Push:** Uploading committed changes from your local copy to GitHub.
- **Pull request (PR):** A request to merge changes from one branch
  into another; the standard review mechanism for collaborative
  repositories.


## Safety and Hazards

This is a computational procedure with no physical hazards.


## Accessing RStudio

### Pomona College RStudio Server

The recommended method for EA Program work:

1. Open a browser and go to `rstudio.pomona.edu`
2. Log in with your Pomona College credentials
3. Your files are stored on the server (no local installation needed)

### Local Installation

Install in this order if working offline:

1. R: [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org/)
2. RStudio Desktop: [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
3. Git: [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/)


## Setting Up GitHub

### Create a GitHub Account

1. Go to [github.com](https://github.com) and create a free account
2. Use your Pomona email address
3. Choose a professional username (e.g., `firstlast` or `flastname`)

### Configure SSH Keys

SSH keys let RStudio communicate with GitHub securely. Set them up
once per machine (or server account).

1. In RStudio, open the Terminal tab
2. Generate a key pair:

   ```bash
   ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_pomona_email@pomona.edu"
   ```

3. Accept the default file location; leave the passphrase blank for
   server use
4. Print the public key:

   ```bash
   cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
   ```

5. Copy the output
6. On GitHub: Settings > SSH and GPG keys > New SSH key > paste and
   save
7. Test the connection:

   ```bash
   ssh -T git@github.com
   ```

   A message beginning "Hi username!" confirms success.


## Working with Repositories

### Clone an Existing Repository

1. On GitHub, navigate to the repository and click **Code > SSH**
2. Copy the SSH URL (`git@github.com:org/repo.git`)
3. In RStudio: File > New Project > Version Control > Git
4. Paste the URL; choose a local directory; click **Create Project**

### The Pull-Edit-Commit-Push Workflow

Always pull before editing to avoid merge conflicts:

1. **Pull:** Click the blue down-arrow in the Git pane (or `git pull`)
2. **Edit:** Make your changes in R scripts or `.qmd` files
3. **Stage:** Check boxes next to changed files in the Git pane
4. **Commit:** Click Commit; write a clear message (e.g.,
   `"Add soil texture analysis for sites 4-6"`)
5. **Pull again:** Pull once more before pushing to catch any
   concurrent changes
6. **Push:** Click the green up-arrow to push to GitHub

### Branching Workflow

For experimental analyses or features that are not yet ready for the
main branch:

```bash
git checkout -b feature/my-analysis   # create and switch to new branch
# ... make changes and commits ...
git push -u origin feature/my-analysis
# Open a Pull Request on GitHub when ready to merge
```


## Writing Quarto Documents

### Rmd vs. Qmd

| Feature          | Rmd                        | Qmd                              |
|:-----------------|:---------------------------|:---------------------------------|
| Maintained by    | RStudio/Posit              | Quarto project (open source)     |
| Requires R       | Yes                        | No (also supports Python, Julia) |
| Chunk options    | In header: `{r, echo=TRUE}` | On lines: `#| echo: true`      |
| SOP system uses  | Legacy                     | Preferred for new documents      |

For new EA Program documents, use `.qmd`. Existing `.Rmd` files will
continue to work.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Common Chunk Options

- `#| echo: true` shows the code in the output (use for teaching)
- `#| echo: false` hides the code (use for reports)
- `#| eval: false` shows the code but does not run it
- `#| fig-cap: "Caption text"` adds a figure caption
- `#| warning: false` suppresses warning messages
:::

## Advanced Topics

### Protecting the Main Branch

For repositories with multiple active contributors, enable branch
protection rules on GitHub:

1. Go to Settings > Branches > Add rule
2. Enter `main` as the branch name pattern
3. Check **Require a pull request before merging**
4. Optionally check **Require approvals** (set to 1)

### GitHub Issues for Task Tracking

Create an issue for each task, assign it to a team member, and close
it when the work is merged. This creates a record of who did what and
when.

### .gitignore

Add file patterns that should never be committed:

```
.Rhistory
.RData
.Rproj.user/
docs/
_freeze/
*.pdf
```

## Training Record

Before using R/RStudio/GitHub independently for EA Program research,
personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Create a GitHub account and configure SSH keys (Sections 11.1--11.3)
3. Successfully clone, pull, edit, commit, and push to the
   `beginnersluck` practice repository (Sections 12--13)
4. Create and render at least one `.qmd` file (Section 17)
5. Demonstrate the Pull-Edit-Commit-Push workflow under supervision
6. Be signed off by the PI or project lead
